- **Adoration (Beloved)** — the chaste Passion of **fine amor / Romance**. The Beloved
  must be **apparently unattainable** and initially rejects the Lover; the Beloved's
  feelings don't matter — inspiration comes from their mere existence, and suffering
  deepens it. Two huge advantages: grants a **+10 Skill bonus regardless of
  Inspiration/Impassionment**, and may be invoked **once per day at any time for any
  reason**. May cause **Misery**; Famous/Exalted Adorers risk **Melancholy** at
  reminders of the Beloved. Requires complete chastity; **becomes Love if consummated**
  (moving to Fervor).
  - **Involuntary Adoration:** on first seeing someone of Transcendent Beauty/power
    (Ygraine, Guenever, Isoud, Lancelot, Tristram…), roll **Lustful, Arbitrary, and
    Honest** — if **all three succeed**, gain Adoration at **1D6** (+5 for Transcendent
    Beauty, +10 for exemplars like Guenever/Galahad). This is the only way to hold more
    than one Adoration at once.
- **Devotion (Deity)** — faith in a supernatural being; confers no knowledge or powers,
  and does **not** count as Directed. Acquired at will but **cannot inspire until the
  character qualifies as a Religious Knight** (p.127); then invoked at blasphemy, abuse
  of a holy place/person, or when championing the religion.

## Civilitas — Chivalry, Hospitality & Station

- **Chivalry** — the strong protect the weak; act honorably toward ladies, commoners,
  and knights. Generated by declaring the desire, but **cannot inspire until qualified
  as a Chivalrous knight**. May conflict with **Station** (resolve by opposed roll).
  Invoked when a chivalric virtue is offended or there's a chance to uphold the Code
  (defend a lady, protect a commoner). The Chivalric Code forbids e.g. missile weapons
  against knights and requires mercy (to deny a hated foe mercy needs a **failed
  Merciful roll**), generosity (sharing Glory with fellows), fairness, and courtesy.
- **Hospitality** — a Universal Passion; offer food/lodging/safety without expectation.
  Inside a hearth, **peace must reign** even between enemies, and a guest must help
  defend it; a guest may not leave without the host's permission, and the host may
  never act against a guest. Invoked by the wronged party when host or guest breaks
  Hospitality, or when a knight witnesses a violation. (Not invoked merely because your
  home is attacked from outside — but yes if an invited guest draws a weapon, or a
  permitted guest is attacked.)
- **Station** — a Universal Passion upholding the social order (king > nobles >
  knights > esquires > commoners). Invoked when witnessing offenses to station (a
  commoner failing deference, taking liberties, or offering violence to nobles; a
  protected commoner attacked by foreigners; a knight rebuked for abusing a commoner; a
  lower noble offending a higher). Knights **lose Honor** by behaving like commoners
  (manual labor, hawking goods, non-holding business). Chivalrous knights often make
  opposed rolls **against** their own Station.

title: Passions of Fidelitas (Duty, Fealty, Homage, Loyalty)
text:
Fidelitas is personal loyalty — always directed at a **person or group** (never a
place, action, animal, artifact, or ideal). Bonds are sealed by oaths; oath-breakers
become permanent outcasts.

- **Duty (Vassals)** — a lord's responsibility to their sworn knights; automatically
  gained whenever others swear Homage/Fealty to you. Invoked when a sworn vassal is in
  danger.
- **Fealty** — the "standard" feudal oath of obedience, sworn on Bible/relics, often
  **time-limited** and expiring without consequence; may be sworn to **multiple**
  lords; **inferior to Homage** (ignored if the two conflict). Mercenaries and
  professionals (stewards, clerks) swear Fealty for their term of service, then may
  serve anyone (even old enemies) without dishonor. Invoked when the lord is threatened
  or someone interferes with a deed done on his behalf.
- **Homage** — the **highest loyalty**, sworn for household membership or a land grant
  (heritable, if heirs also swear). One liege lord takes primacy over lesser homages.
  **Violating Homage is penalized more than any other loyalty — refusal loses Honor**
  (see [[core.aspirations.honor]]). Invoked when the liege or family is threatened,
  someone interferes with a deed for the lord, or the liege's Honor is impugned.
  - **Ending Homage/Fealty** never happens during a military expedition, only between
    wars: by *mutual agreement* (often generating a **Favor** to the releasing lord; a
    knight transferring up owes the new lord a Favor equal to the new Standard of
    Living); by *liege's choice* (needs serious cause; knight may demand trial by peers
    or combat); or by *knight's choice* (made public at court, returning gifts,
    declaring the lord's oath-violation; a resentful lord may name them enemy, granting
    **40 days' safe conduct**). A departing vassal keeps family lands but must quickly
    find a new liege or risk seizure.
- **Loyalty (Companions)** — mutual bond among a group of unrelated individuals (e.g. a
  band of PKs); list the members. Invoked when a companion is threatened, endangered,
  or fighting alongside.
- **Loyalty (King)** — loyalty to a king who isn't one's liege. If a vassal is more
  loyal to a king than their own lord, the lord may develop a **Jealousy** Obsession.
  It doesn't excuse feudal duty; escape requires formally breaking one's oath or being
  invited to serve the king directly. Invoked when the king/family is threatened,
  someone interferes with a deed for the king, or the king's Honor is impugned.

title: Passions — Nature, Levels, Courts, Raising/Lowering & Battle Use
text:
**Passions** are deeply-held beliefs/emotions that can inspire legendary feats or
coerce a character against their interests. They may grant temporary modifiers to
**Skills and Traits** — never to Characteristics or other Passions.

## Gaining a new Passion

Players may request one, or the GM may assign one when warranted (family murder →
Hate; rescue → Loyalty; miracle → Devotion). A new Passion starts at **1D6+6** (GM
may adjust). Too many Famous/Exalted Passions can cripple a knight (Lancelot's Love vs
Homage).

## Passion levels

- **Unsung** 1–4 · **Normal** 5–15 · **Famous** 16–20 · **Exalted** 20+x.
- A **Famous** Passion triggers easily (less autonomy); an **Exalted** Passion must
  always be acted upon (rare).

## Courts (40-point cap each)

Passions belong to four courts — **Fidelitas, Fervor, Adoratio, Civilitas** — plus
**Honor** (stands alone). **The sum of all Passions in a court may not exceed 40.**
Raising one Passion in a full court forces another in that court **down** (player's
choice), unless the rising one is already at 20.

**Directed Passions** are focused on a specific object (like Directed Traits).
Devotion (Deity) explicitly does **not** count as Directed.

## Raising & lowering

- **Raise:** gain a check and roll above the value in the Winter Phase, or add a
  Prestige Reward.
- **Lower (permanent):** a fumbled Passion roll (−1); a fumbled Passion Crisis roll
  (−1); a Prestige Reward; court-cap displacement; or **deliberately violating** the
  Passion.

**Violating a Passion:** to act against its reason (secretly meeting your lord's
enemy while holding Loyalty (Lord)) requires a **failed Passion roll** and reduces the
Passion by 1. Exalted Passions can't be failed this way unless modifiers drop them
below 20.

## Passions in battle

Each Passion may inspire **once per battle** (multi-day battles like Badon may allow
more). A knight does **not** get Homage/Loyalty (King) merely because their liege is
present — only if the liege is in **immediate danger**. When to roll **Hate** depends
on the enemy army's composition (vs a Saxon army, a Famous/Exalted Hate (Saxons) lets
the knight choose the round; vs Saxon mercenaries in a Cymric army, it must be rolled
on first contact).

**GM characters** generally don't use Passions early on, but should later in a
campaign and whenever a nameless knight defends their own home/liege.

title: Traits & Trait Rolls (Decision/Test/Hint, Valorous Roll, Religious Virtues)
text:
Traits are paired emotions (summing to 20) that influence Honor, Glory, and
behavior. A character tends to act on the higher Trait. **Normal (5–15)** Traits
allow the most freedom; **Famous (16–20)** and **Exalted (20+x)** Traits increasingly
compel behavior. A critical or fumble on a Trait roll may grant a **+5 to a
subsequent Skill or Passion roll**.

## Trait Roll results

Roll 1D20 against the Trait. Famous/Exalted Traits **must be rolled first**; an
unmodified Exalted Trait never fails.

- **Critical** — acts strongly per the Trait; take a check; GM may grant +5 to a
  later Skill/Passion roll.
- **Success** — acts per the Trait; check only if significant.
- **Failure** — roll again against the **Opposing Trait** (with modifiers). If that
  also fails, the player acts as they wish.
- **Fumble** — acts strongly per the **Opposing Trait** and checks it; GM may grant
  the +5.

**Opposing Trait roll:** Critical → acts strongly per opposing Trait (+check, +5);
Success → acts per opposing Trait; Failure → player's choice; Fumble → acts strongly
per the **original** Trait (+check, +5).

Modifiers apply to the Trait value (large/horrifying creatures often impose −Valorous;
this can drop an Exalted Trait below 20, forcing a roll).

## Trait Rolls in Play (three ways)

- **Decision rolls** — decide behavior. Not truly opposed: if the first roll
  succeeds, the second isn't made. Player picks which side to test first (except a
  Famous Trait must be tested first if acting against it; an Exalted Trait offers no
  choice).
- **Test rolls** — unopposed moral/spiritual trials (a *Just* roll to answer a justice
  riddle; an *Indulgent* roll to avoid getting drunk). Some tests just compare the
  **value** (Honest 15+ to reach Avalon; a shield only an Exaltedly Chaste knight may
  bear).
- **Game hint rolls** — GM prompts ("Suspicious characters get a roll here"); success
  = check, and an Opposing Trait roll follows a failure.

## Influencing another character

An **opposed Trait vs Trait** roll. If the influencer wins, the target takes an
automatic check in the influencing Trait; if the influencer loses, they make an
immediate Opposing Trait roll for a check. The winning Trait dictates the action; a
tie is no result. This can **diminish another's Famous/Exalted Trait**.

**Traits opposing Passions:** a Trait may oppose a Passion (own or another's) via an
opposed roll; the loser may make an Opposing Trait roll for a check.

## The Valorous Roll

A fairy or beast with a **Valorous Modifier** cannot be attacked until the character
makes a **Valorous roll** (a Test Roll — everyone rolls, even Unsung/Normal),
adjusted by the modifier, on sighting it. **Fail** → hesitate one Combat Round, may
retry. **Fumble** → flee the scene.

## Religious Virtues (16+ in all six → Religious Knight boon, p.127)

- **Christian:** Chaste, Forgiving, Merciful, Modest, Spiritual, Temperate
- **Pagan:** Energetic, Generous, Honest, Lustful, Proud, Spiritual
- **Wodinic:** Generous, Indulgent, Proud, Reckless, Valorous, Worldly
- **Heathen:** Arbitrary, Honest, Proud, Spiritual, Suspicious, Vengeful

title: Feasting (Feasts & Banquets event)
text:
Feasts are major social set-pieces, treated on par with tournaments as a vehicle
for interactions, schemes, rivalries, and alliances. A "feast" may be a holy/market
day, a wedding or knighting, or just the meal itself. Play runs as a series of
abstract **Feast Rounds**, each resolved around **Geniality** and **Feast Events**.

## Geniality

**Geniality** is a modifier measuring one's nobility in peers' eyes. Add it to
**APP** and most **Courtly Skills** (Compose, Courtesy, Dancing, Fashion,
Flirting, Gaming, Intrigue, Orate, Play Instrument, Singing) at court or during a
feast. It also modifies **everyone else's Recognize** roll made about that knight
in a courtly setting.

- Starting Geniality is set by the knight's **clothing** (based on Standard of
  Living + Fashion skill if applied). Lords maintain their knights at **Ordinary**
  level by default.
- **Geniality can never exceed the character's APP.**

**Clothing → Geniality (Table 3.1, Class Minimum column):**

| Class minimum | Clothing cost | Geniality |
|---|---|---|
| (a few denarii) | few d. | −5 |
| Mercenary Knight (no squire) | 120 d. | −3 |
| Mercenary Knight | £1 | +1 |
| Household / Vassal Knight | £2 | +2 |
| Estate Holder | £4 | +3 |
| Banneret | £8 | +4 |
| Baron | £16 | +5 |
| Rich Baron | £32 | +6 |
| Count, Duke, Minor King | — | — |

Knights may always dress **above** their station if they can afford it; the Class
Minimum is the floor for that rank.

## Feast Rounds

Each Round ≈ 1–2 hours of eating, mixing, revelry, and private talk. The GM sets
the number of Rounds up front by feast size (**Table 3.2**, suggested minimums):

| Size | Example | Min. Rounds |
|---|---|---|
| Small | A vassal knight's wedding | 2 |
| Medium | A neighborhood tournament's closing feast | 3 |
| Large | Easter feast for a duke | 4 |
| Royal | Arthur's Pentecost feast | 5 |

## Seating — "the Salt"

Seating is by **rank first, then Glory**; special circumstances can promote a
character but **never** by random roll. Four areas, relative to the salt cellar at
the high table (per-Round Geniality effect):

- **Above the Salt** (high table): **+2 Geniality/Round**, but **all Geniality
  losses from Events are doubled** ("all eyes on you").
- **Closer to the Salt** (lower table, near its head): **+1 Geniality/Round**.
- **Farther from the Salt** (default for most guests): no modifier.
- **On the Floor** (squires, dogs, snubbed guests): **−1 Geniality/Round**, or
  **−2/Round** if seated here through a fumbled Glory roll.

Telling a knight to sit lower than before is an insult; seating them among squires
or commoners is grave enough to justify breaking with a lord.

### The Glory Roll (seating placement)
Before the feast each knight makes one **unopposed Glory roll** (vs. Glory ÷ 1000).
Feast size shifts the result: **small feast → move up one level of success; royal
feast → move down one level** (no worse than Farther from the Salt unless fumbled).

**Table 3.3 — Feast Seating:**

| Result | Seating |
|---|---|
| Critical | Above the Salt |
| Success | Closer to the Salt |
| Failure | Farther from the Salt |
| Fumble | Re-roll Glory (this time a fumble counts as a simple failure), then take a seat **one position further down** than the re-roll gives. If that lands on Farther from the Salt, you **eat on the floor** with the dogs and squires. |

### Effects on Honor
A knight involuntarily seated **below** a same-rank knight who has **fewer Glory**
must pass a **Modest** test or lose **1 Honor**. Fumbling the Glory roll — or
having a **Famous/Exalted Proud** value — inflicts that 1 Honor loss automatically.

### Ceding your position
A character may **voluntarily** cede to a lower area (to sit with comrades) via a
**Modest** test: success → check Modest and **gain 10 Glory** (**20** on a
critical), then move down; failure → the move can't be arranged; fumble → it reads
as disingenuous, costing **1 Honor**. Characters with Famous/Exalted Proud **may
not** cede.

## Feast Events (cards)

Each Round, each knight totals **APP + Geniality + a Glory prominence bonus**
(Table 3.4). That **Total APP** sets how many Feast Event Cards may be drawn
(Table 3.5).

**Table 3.4 — Glory Prominence Modifier:**

| Glory | Title | Modifier |
|---|---|---|
| 0–999 | Non-knight | +0 |
| 1,000–2,999 | Unproven | +1 |
| 3,000–3,999 | Veteran | +2 |
| 4,000–5,999 | Respected | +3 |
| 6,000–7,999 | Notable | +4 |
| 8,000–11,999 | Renowned | +5 |
| 12,000–15,999 | Illustrious | +6 |
| 16,000–31,999 | Extraordinary | +7 |
| 32,000+ | Legendary | +8 |

**Table 3.5 — Feast Event Cards by APP:**

| Total APP | Events/Round |
|---|---|
| 4− | 0 |
| 5–9 | 1 |
| 10–14 | 2 |
| 15–19 | 3 |
| 20–24 | 4 |
| 25–29 | 5 |
| 30+ | 6 |

**Drawing rules:**
- Draw **one card at a time**, then either play it or draw again up to the Total
  APP limit. **The last card must always be played**, even if harmful.
- Total APP can rise mid-feast (from Geniality gains), unlocking more draws.
- A **Host Event Card** (goblet symbol) must be **played immediately** and ends
  drawing for that Round.
- Unplayed cards are reshuffled; played cards are set aside until the deck is
  exhausted, then reshuffled in.

**Reading a card:** most call for an opposed/unopposed Statistic roll — follow the
card and apply results at once. Some cards are kept across Rounds for a bonus; some
trigger rolls from every other attendee (each resolves individually). The **number
at the bottom is the Geniality modifier** gained on playing the card, applied
regardless of the card's other dice results; your Geniality changes only when the
card is put in play.

### The Feast Event Card deck (catalogue)

*Source: Chaosium's printable Feast Event Cards (`pendragon_printable_feast_cards.pdf`,
a separate deck to the GM handbook). The physical deck has multiple copies of some
cards; the unique cards are listed below with their **Roll/Test** and **base
Geniality** (the number printed at the card's foot). Card types:*

- **Host cards** (goblet symbol) — play **immediately** on draw; no further draws
  that Round. These are the *Host …* and *Meet the Host* cards; several convene the
  **whole hall** (all Player-characters roll).
- **Keeper cards** — kept in play for an ongoing effect; most **stop you drawing**
  other cards while held.
- **All-players cards** — trigger a roll from every attendee (the "More Drink /
  More Food" and *Host Calls …* family).

Several cards defer to other systems: the **Intoxication rules** (drink cards),
**duel** challenges, and Winter-Phase gains (e.g. a SIZ increase).

### Other Events (no card)
A knight who won't risk a card instead picks one of four activities — **Gossiping,
flirting, gaming, or eating/drinking** — and rolls unopposed vs. the relevant
Skill/Trait (**Flirting, Gaming, Intrigue, or Indulgent**), modified by Geniality.
**Success** → a check to that Skill/Trait; **critical** → also earn **Glory equal
to Total APP**. Use **Table 3.6: Random Feast Courses** (1D20 per course, three
courses) to generate a "favorite dish" or add colour.

## Departing the Feast

**Failing to attend at all** when invited is a grave insult — attend for at least
one Round or risk dire consequences. After the first Round, a knight may retire by
**begging leave** with a **Courtesy** roll:
- **Success:** a check; **critical:** also **+10 Glory**. Host is gratified.
- **Failure:** dismissed curtly; **lose 1D3 Geniality** (min 0).
- **Fumble:** left without leave / gave offence; **lose 1 Honor and all
  accumulated Geniality**.

**Forced Departure:** some Event Cards drag a knight out early (passing out drunk,
napping after excess, leaving with a lover). These need **no Courtesy roll**, but
others notice and it may still cost Honor at the GM's discretion.

## Feasting Glory (end of feast)

At the last Round, total the **Geniality gained solely from Feast Events** (exclude
starting Geniality) and compare to **Table 3.7**:

- **Below threshold:** Glory = (**Appeal + Geniality**) × **Rounds attended**,
  **max 100 Glory**.
- **Meets/exceeds threshold:** that Glory **plus the bonus** (standout guest). If
  several beat it, the **highest accumulated Geniality** wins the bonus; ties go to
  **highest Glory**.

**Table 3.7 — Geniality Threshold:**

| Size | Threshold | Bonus Glory |
|---|---|---|
| Small | 5 | +10 |
| Medium | 7 | +25 |
| Large | 9 | +50 |
| Royal | 11 | +100 |

*Example: at a medium feast Sir Avalloc (APP 11) accrues 6 Geniality → (11+6)×3 =
**51 Glory**. With 8 Geniality (beating the threshold of 7) → 51 + 25 = **76
Glory** as the standout guest.*
